chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Salih ibn Sa'd al-Tamimi informed us. He said: Musa ibn Dawud narrated to us. He said: al-Walid ibn Hisham narrated to us. He said: Hisham ibn Hassan narrated to us from al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Basri from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm al-Dawsi. He said:

Mu'adh ibn Jabal visited the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) weeping. He greeted him and he returned the greeting. Then he said: What makes you cry, O Mu'adh? He said: O Messenger of Allah, at the door there is a youth with a soft body, pure complexion, and good appearance, weeping over his youth as a bereaved mother weeps over her child, and he wants to enter upon you. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: Let the youth enter, O Mu'adh. So he brought him in, and he greeted him and he returned the greeting. Then he said: What makes you cry, O youth?

He said: How can I not cry when I have committed sins such that if Allah, Mighty and Majestic, were to take me for some of them, He would cast me into the Fire of Hell, and I see nothing but that He will take me for them, and will never forgive me. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Have you associated any partners with Allah? He said: I seek refuge in Allah from associating anything with my Lord. He said: Have you killed a soul that Allah has prohibited? He said: No. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: May Allah forgive your sins, even if they were like the great mountains. The youth said: Surely they are greater than the great mountains. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: May Allah forgive your sins, even if they were like the seven earths, their oceans, their sands, their trees, and all creatures therein. He said: Surely they are greater than the seven earths, their oceans, their sands, their trees, and all creatures therein. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: May Allah forgive your sins, even if they were like the seven heavens and their stars, and like the Throne and the Seat. He said: Surely they are greater than that.

So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) looked at him angrily, then said: Woe to you, O youth! Are your sins greater, or your Lord? So the youth fell on his face saying: Glory be to my Lord! Nothing is greater than my Lord. My Lord is greater, O Prophet of Allah, than every great thing. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: Can anyone other than the Great Lord forgive the great sin?! The youth said: No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah. Then the youth went silent. So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: Woe to you, O youth! Will you not tell me of one of your sins?

He said: Of course, I will tell you. I was a grave robber for seven years. I would exhume the dead and take their shrouds. A young woman from the daughters of the Ansar died. When she was carried to her grave, buried, and her family left, and night fell, I came to her grave and exhumed her. Then I took her out and removed her shrouds, leaving her bare at the edge of her grave. I went to leave, but Satan came to me and began making her attractive to me, saying: Do you not see her stomach and her whiteness? Do you not see her hips? He did not stop saying this until I returned to her, and I could not control myself until I had relations with her and left her in her place. Then I heard a voice from behind me saying: O youth, woe to you from the Judge of the Day of Judgment, the day He raises me and you just as you left me naked among the dead, exhumed me from my grave, stripped my shrouds, and left me in ritual impurity before my Judgment. Woe to your youth from the Fire. I do not think I shall ever smell the scent of Paradise. What do you see for me, O Messenger of Allah?

So the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: Get away from me, O wicked one! I fear that I will get burned by your fire. How near you are to the Fire! How near you are to the Fire! Then he (peace be upon him and his family) did not stop speaking and pointing at him until the youth left his presence. He went to Medina, gathered provisions from it, then went to one of its mountains to worship therein. He wore a hair cloak,

and bound his hands together to his neck, and called out: O Lord, this is Your servant Bahlul, bound before You. O Lord, You are the One who knows me, and my errors that You know of. O my Master, O Lord, I have become one of the regretful, and I came to Your Prophet repentant, but he sent me away and increased my fear. So I ask You by Your name, Your majesty, and the greatness of Your power, do not diminish my hope, my Master, and do not invalidate my supplication, and do not deprive me of Your mercy. He did not stop saying this for forty days and nights. The wild animals and beasts would weep for him. When forty days and nights had passed, he raised his hands to the sky and said: O Allah, what will You do regarding my need? If You have accepted my supplication and forgiven my sin, then send revelation to Your Prophet. And if You have not accepted my supplication and not forgiven my sin, and You want my punishment, then hasten a fire to burn me or a punishment in this world to destroy me, and deliver me from the disgrace of the Day of Resurrection.

So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed to His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): 'And those who, when they commit an indecency' — meaning fornication — 'or wrong themselves' — meaning by committing a sin greater than fornication, grave robbing, and taking shrouds — 'remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins' — meaning they feared Allah and hastened to repent — 'and who can forgive sins except Allah?' He said, Mighty and Majestic: My servant came to you repentant, O Muhammad, and you sent him away. Where would he go, to whom would he turn, and whom would he ask to forgive his sin besides Me? Then He said, Mighty and Majestic: 'and those who do not persist in what they have done while they know' — meaning they no longer commit fornication, grave robbing, or taking shrouds — 'their reward is forgiveness from their Lord and gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they shall abide eternally, and excellent is the reward of the doers of good' (3:135-136).

When this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), he went out reciting it and smiling. He said to his companions: Who will direct me to that repentant youth? Mu'adh said: O Messenger of Allah, we were told he is in such-and-such place. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) went with his companions until they reached that mountain. They climbed it searching for the youth, and there they found the youth standing between two rocks, his hands bound to his neck, his face blackened, his eyelashes fallen from weeping, and he was saying:

My Master, You have perfected my form and made my appearance beautiful. So I wish I knew what You intend for me — will You burn me in the Fire, or will You settle me in Your proximity? O Allah, You have bestowed much goodness upon me and blessed me. So I wish I knew what my end will be — will You escort me to Paradise, or drive me to the Fire? O Allah, my sin is greater than the heavens and the earth, and Your vast Seat and Your great Throne. So I wish I knew — will You forgive my sin, or will You scandalize me with it on the Day of Resurrection? He did not stop saying things like this while weeping and pouring dust on his head. The wild animals surrounded him and the birds lined up above him, weeping at his weeping. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) drew near, freed his hands from his neck, cleaned the dust from his head, and said: O Bahlul, rejoice, for you have been freed by Allah from the Fire.

Then he (peace be upon him and his family) said to his companions: This is how you redress your sins, just as Bahlul redressed them. Then he recited to him what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed about him and gave him glad tidings of Paradise.

key_terms.عتيق الله: One freed by Allah from the Fire

ai.seo_question: What is the story of Bahlul who repented for grave robbing in Islamic hadith?
ai.summary: A dramatic narrative in which a youth named Bahlul comes to the Prophet (SAWW) in deep anguish over his grievous sins of grave robbing and desecrating a corpse. After the Prophet initially sends him away in horror, Bahlul retreats to the mountains for forty days of intense repentance, binding himself and crying out to Allah. In response, Allah reveals Quran 3:135-136, affirming that sincere repentance is accepted regardless of the magnitude of the sin, and the Prophet joyfully seeks out Bahlul to deliver the glad tidings of forgiveness.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq (rh) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Hamadani narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Salih b. Sa`d al-Tamimi informed us. He said: Musa b. Dawud narrated to us. He said: Al-Walid b. Hisham narrated to us. He said: Hisham b. Hassan narrated to us from al-Hasan b. Abi'l Hasan al-Basri from `Abd al-Rahman b. Ghanam al-Dusi. He said: Mu`adh b.

Jabal visited the Messenger of Allah (s) weeping. He greeted him with the salaam and he responded with the salaam. Then, he said: Why are you crying, O Mu`adh? So, he said: O Messenger of Allah! At the door, there is a youth who has a good physique, a clean complexion, and a good appearance. He is weeping over his youthhood as a bereaved mother weeps over her child, and he wants to visit you. So, the Prophet (s) said: Let the youth enter, O Mu`adh. So, he let him enter, and he greeted him with the salaam and he responded with the salaam. Then, he said: What is causing you to cry, O youth?

He said: How can I not cry when I have committed sins that Allah would send me to the Fire of Hell for just one of them? He will not see me except that He will take me and never forgive me. So, the Messenger of Allah (s) said: Have you associated any partners with Allah? He said: I seek refuge in Allah that I should associate any partners with my Lord. He said: Did you kill a soul that Allah has prohibited you from killing? He said: No. So, the Prophet (s) said: May Allah forgive your sins, even if they are like large mountains. So, the youth said: Surely, they are greater than large mountains. So, the Prophet (s) said: May Allah forgive your sins, even if they are like the seven Earths, their oceans, their grains of sand, their trees, and whatever is in them. He said: Surely, they are greater than the seven Earths, their oceans, their grains of sand, their trees, and whatever is in them. So, the Prophet (s) said: May Allah forgive your sins, even if they are like the seven heavens and its stars, even if they are like the Throne and the Seat.

He said: They are greater than that.  He said: So, the Prophet (s) looked at him angrily, then said: Beware, O youth. What is greater, your sins or your Lord? So, the youth fell on his face, saying: May my Lord be glorified! There is nothing greater than my Lord. My Lord is greater, O Prophet of Allah, than every great thing. So, the Prophet (s) said: Can anyone other than the great Lord forgive a great sin?! The youth said: No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah. Then, the youth went silent. So, the Prophet (s) said to him: Woe to you, O youth! Will you inform me of one of your sins?

He said: Of course, I will inform you. I was a grave robber for seven years. I would exhume the dead and take off their shrouds. A young woman from the girls of the Ansar had died. When she was carried to her grave and buried, her family left, and night came. I came to her grave, exhumed her, and took from her shrouds. I left her alone at the edge of her grave. Time passed, and Satan came to me, and he began to make her more pleasing to me, saying: "Did you see her stomach and her whiteness? Did you see her hips?" He did not stop saying this to me until I returned to her. I could not control myself, until I had intercourse with her and left her in her place. Then, I heard a voice from behind me, saying: "O youth! Beware of the debts of the Day of Religion; the day you and I will be raised. You left me naked on the frontiers of death, emptied me from my grave, took my shrouds, and left me in a state of impurity until my Judgment. Woe to your youthhood from the Fire."  So, I do not think that I will ever smell the scent of Paradise. What do you see for me, O Messenger of Allah?

So, the Prophet (s) said: Get away from me, O wretched one! Surely, I fear that I will get burned by your fire. How near you are to the Fire, how near you are to the Fire!  He (s) did not stop speaking to him and pointing to him until he left his presence and went to Medina, picked up some things from it, and went to one of its mountains to worship therein; wearing a cloak made of hair.

He bound his hands together to his neck and called: O Lord! This is your servant, Bahlul, and I am bound before You. O Lord! You are the one that knows me and my errors. O my Master, O Lord! I have become regretful, and I have come repentant to Your Prophet, but he sent me away and increased my fear. So, I ask You by Your name, Your majesty, and the greatness of Your power, to not diminish my hope, my Master; and to not invalidate my supplication, and to not deprive me of Your mercy. He did not stop saying this for forty days and nights. The lions and the beasts would weep for him. When forty days and nights had passed, he raised his hands to the sky and said: O Allah! What will you do regarding my need? Have you accepted my supplication and forgiven my mistake? If so, then send a revelation to Your Prophet. But, if You will not answer my supplication nor forgive my mistake, then I want my punishment; so, bring a fire that will burn me or a punishment in this world that will destroy me. Deliver me from the furor of the Day of Resurrection.

So, Allah revealed to His Prophet (s): "As for those who perform indecency" - meaning, fornication - "or wrong themselves" - meaning, commit a sin greater than fornication, grave robbing, and stealing shrouds - "remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins" - meaning, those who fear Allah and quickly repent - "who can forgive sins except Allah?" [3:135]. He said: "My servant came to you repentant, O Muhammad, and you sent him away. So, where would he go, who should he seek, and who should he seek forgiveness for his sin besides Me?" Then, He said: "[and those] who do not persist in what they have done once they become cognizant." [3:135] - meaning, they no longer commit fornication, nor exhume graves, nor steal shrouds - "their reward is with their Lord - gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally - excellent is the reward of the doers of good" [3:136].

When this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (s), he came out reciting it and smiling. So, he said to his companions: Who will direct me to that repentant youth? So, Mu`adh said: O Messenger of Allah! We were told that he was in such-and-such place. So, the Messenger of Allah (s) went with his companions until they ended up at that mountain; and they climbed it in search of the youth. They found the youth standing between two rocks with his hands bound to his neck. His face was blackened, and his eyelashes had fallen from weeping.

He was saying: “O my Master! You have perfected my form, and made my form beautiful, so what will You do with me? Will You burn me in the Fire, or will You settle me in Your proximity? O Allah! You have bestowed me with much goodness, and You have blessed me; so, what will be my end – will You dress me in Paradise, or have me driven by the Fire? O Allah! My mistake is greater than the heavens, the Earth, Your widespread Seat and Your great Throne. So, will You forgive my mistake, or will You scandalize me with it on the Day of Resurrection?”  He did not stop saying this, weeping and covering his head with dust. The lions surrounded him, and the birds lined up above him, weeping at his weeping. So, the Messenger of Allah (s) came close, took his hands off his neck, and cleaned the dust off his head, and said: O Bahlul! Be happy, for Allah has freed you from the Fire.
Then, he (s) said to his companions: This is how you redress your sins, just as Bahlul redressed them. Then, he recited what Allah revealed to him, and gave him glad tidings of Paradise.
